issueTitle: Show a count of remaining todos

plan.summary: Add a "N left" counter under the todo list in `apps/web/src/App.tsx`, derived from the existing `todos` state (so it updates on add/toggle/delete with no extra state), with the count/label logic extracted to a new pure module `apps/web/src/remaining.ts` and covered by a plain `.ts` Vitest test that fits the repo's existing test setup.

ambiguities.detail: Whether the counter counts not-done todos only (issue's example implies it, but the exact definition of "remaining" vs. total is inferred from one worked example)
Exact placement and markup/styling of the counter element (which tag, class, position relative to the list container)
Whether the counter should render when todos exist but all are done (i.e. "0 left" shown vs. hidden) — the issue only specifies the no-todos-at-all case
Whether the logic lives inline in App.tsx or is extracted into a separate module (the plan invents `apps/web/src/remaining.ts`)
Whether tests are expected, and at what level (pure unit test of the label function vs. component/DOM test of the rendered UI)

clarity.rationale: The issue gives concrete, example-driven, externally checkable outcomes for count, pluralization, empty state, and reactivity; the remaining open points are minor presentation/structure choices plus the unstated all-done "0 left" case, which the plan silently decided.

objections.detail: The only piece of logic that can actually regress is untested. `countRemaining` (a `.filter().length`) and `remainingLabel` (a template string) are trivially correct; the interesting rule — "with no todos at all the counter is not rendered" — lives as a bare `todos.length > 0` guard inside JSX with no test at all, and the repo has no DOM test setup to catch it (verified: root `vitest.config.ts:5` includes only `apps/**/*.test.ts` / `packages/**/*.test.ts`, and `apps/web` has no jsdom/@testing-library dep). CLAUDE.md:45 requires "New or changed behavior is covered by a test in the same package", and the plan's test covers the arithmetic while the acceptance criterion goes uncovered. Collapsing the two exports into one `remainingLabel(todos: readonly Todo[]): string | null` that returns `null` for an empty array would put the empty-list criterion under unit test, shrink App.tsx to `{remainingLabel(todos)}`... plus a truthiness guard, and drop a redundant export — better fit for the repo's "keep it small" instruction (CLAUDE.md:7-8) than a two-function module.

Step 2 tells the implementer to write a fixture factory annotated `: Todo` but never says how `Todo` is imported in the test file; the `import type` requirement is called out only for `remaining.ts` (step 1 and the risks list). `apps/web/tsconfig.json:8` includes `src`, so `remaining.test.ts` is type-checked, and `tsconfig.base.json:10` sets `verbatimModuleSyntax` — a plain `import { Todo } from "@todos/shared"` there makes `pnpm typecheck` fail. Spell out `import type { Todo } from "@todos/shared";` in step 2 as well.

Step 4 says to give `.remaining` "the same muted treatment" as `.empty` and then specifies a different value: `.empty` is `opacity: 0.5` (verified, `apps/web/src/styles.css:92-94`), the plan writes `opacity: 0.6`. Trivial, but if the intent is consistency, use 0.5.
